newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IMF's Camdessus sees no snowballing of Thai crisis.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus sees no snowballing of Thai crisis.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) chief Michel Camdessus chided Thai regulators for lax supervision but sought to reassure jittery investors by predicting no repeat of a Mexican peso-style crisis.
He said the IMF had held talks with Thai regulators and he was confident in their ability to handle the problem.

"What they are doing is exactly what you must do to avoid the recurrence of a Mexico-like crisis," Camdessus told an IMF-Hong Kong Monetary Authority Conference on financial integration in Asia and the role of Hong Kong.
"We are ready to continue assisting them in this effort and I don't see any particular reason for this crisis to develop further."
Thai regulators on Monday sent shockwaves through the nation's fragile financial sector by ordering a sigificant revamp.

They ordered 10 finance firms facing liquidity problems to boost their capital by more than $300 million and instructed banks and finance companies to boost provisions against bad loans, particularly for those to the depressed property sector.
The result was a run on deposits at the 10 troubled companies and a stock market plunge which dragged the market down to a near 4-1/2 year low.
Camdessus, managing director of the IMF, described the woes as the flipside of Thailand's successful efforts to overcome poverty and join the ranks of the emerging Asian economies, or Little Tigers.
"The Thai authorities are taking gradual steps to address the kind of tensions which is only the other face of a very successful development policy," he said at the conference.
Camdessus was quoted by the South China Morning Post newspaper as saying Thailand's difficulties stemmed from less-than-rigorous policies and supervision of the country's financial institutions.
He told the conference the authorities were aware of those shortcomings.

"I see them taking steps to address one of the vulnerabilities of the Thai economy... and after recently discussing with them I am confident that the measures and the programme for the future will have the potential to carry the economy back on track for sustainable growth," he said.
He said Thailand was not alone in lacking a developed regulatory framework.
"In many countries in Asia and elsewhere, prudential regulation and supervision have not kept pace with the new complexities of banking business," he said.
Capital inflows and the speed of financial integration and innovation posed new challenges to emerging Asian economies with their fledgling regulatory systems.
"The presence of large capital inflows reduces the room for policy manoeuvre and limits the scope for policy mistakes," Camdessus said.
There was no substitute for stable macroeconomic policies -- policies that give confidence to financial markets and attract private savings, Camdessus said.
